answer: To prevent a haven for disposable identities, admit a voting key only after it solves 1,000 sequential hash puzzles derived from its public key, a fresh beacon and each prior solution. A verifier checks the chain cheaply. Even at the zenith of parallel hardware, 1,000 fake keys require 1,000 distinct chains: sharing solutions fails. Reaching the voting summit therefore costs computation per identity, rather than just account creation.
